appraisal_events.evidence: 'la sincérité et le désintéressement de Saint-Loup étaient... absolus'; his rough treatment of his coachman 'prouvait... moins le sentiment de la différence que de l'égalité entre les classes'; his own words to the narrator: 'N'est-il pas mon égal?... Vous parlez comme un aristocrate,' ajouta-t-il avec dédain.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator affirms Saint-Loup's genuine moral egalitarianism, correcting both Françoise's and the narrator's own more conventional assumptions, while Saint-Loup pointedly rebukes the narrator's aristocratic framing.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'Une carpe, me dit-il, comme toutes ses pareilles. C'est d'ailleurs un peu ma cousine.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup curtly dismisses the princess, but the narrator frames this within his own noted 'prévention et... partialité' against the aristocracy, undercutting the judgment as biased rather than objective.

appraisal_events.evidence: His family and the Faubourg condemn his mistress as having 'dévoyé' him and fear he will be 'déclassé'; but the narrator insists 'tout cela échappait à la famille en larmes': she 'avait mis du sérieux dans sa vie, des délicatesses dans son cœur... l'avait préservé du snobisme,' and Saint-Loup shows the narrator special, unprompted warmth ('s'arrangea à les quitter un peu plus tôt afin de rester seul et en dernier avec moi').
appraisal_events.explanation: Though family and society condemn the liaison as degrading him, the narrator insists it has in fact morally and emotionally refined Saint-Loup, evidenced by his genuine tenderness and special consideration toward the narrator.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'elle l'avait pris en horreur et le torturait'; 'elle avait commencé... à le trouver bête et ridicule'; 'à son mépris pour Saint-Loup s'ajouta la même haine'; meanwhile 'Saint-Loup faisait pour elle de tels sacrifices.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup's mistress has turned to open contempt and cruelty toward him even as he continues sacrificing financially for her, leaving him tormented and powerless in the relationship.

status_effects.explanation: The passage builds a strongly positive portrait of Saint-Loup's sincerity, class egalitarianism, and the genuine moral refinement his liaison has given him.
A countervailing note: the narrator flags Saint-Loup's reflexive prejudice against the aristocracy as a real flaw in his judgment.
He is scorned, tormented, and financially exploited by a mistress who now openly despises him, with no reciprocal power in the relationship.
Saint-Loup visibly corrects and rebukes the narrator's more conventional class assumption, delivered 'avec dédain.'
Saint-Loup singles the narrator out for unprompted personal warmth and consideration, distinguishing him from others.
The narrator states she was equally wrong about Saint-Loup's supposed contempt for the working class, her judgment exposed as another misreading.
Dismissed by Saint-Loup as an interchangeable, unremarkable aristocrat ('une carpe'), though the judgment is framed as biased.

ambiguities: Saint-Loup's mistress, central to E3 and E4, is never named in this passage (only 'sa maîtresse'/'une actrice'); she is not resolved to a canonical character here.
